# Findings about the BRD from the session that settled the backend spec

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Session | Brainstorming backend technical spec, started 03/10/2026 |
| Documents examined | `brd/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.5.md` (abbreviation: BRD), `brd/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.1.md` (addendum), `wireframes/manifest.json`, `wireframes/wireframes-digest.md` (digest), `brand/style-guide.md`, `spec/2026-10-03-frontend-technical-spec.md` (front-end spec) |
| Principle | This session does not edit the BRD. Each row records one gap, contradiction or ambiguity, with evidence by file and line number, the consequence for the backend, and the provisional assumption that the backend spec uses until the product owner decides |
| Status | Being filled in step by step during the session. The "provisional assumption" column is the writer's proposal, not yet settled by the product owner |

Type key: **Missing** (a requirement needs a definition that the document does not have), **Contradiction** (two places say opposite things), **Ambiguous** (can be read two ways), **Inconsistent** (the same thing is listed differently), **Terminology mismatch**, **Outdated label**.

## 1. Findings about the BRD and the addendum

| Id | Type | Content | Evidence | Consequence for the backend | Provisional assumption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF-01 | Missing | **The health formula is not in section 12.** Section 12.1 has 23 definitions, all of them counts and date comparisons. `OVW-05` requires health to be computable along four dimensions (delivery, risk, resource, financial); `EXE-03` requires portfolio health; `MVP-03` takes "the worst of the four dimensions" but does not say how each dimension is computed; `BR-08` mentions "critical risk rules" without listing the rules. Wireframe 14 prints a score of 73/100 together with four dimension scores; wireframe 19 prints a risk score formula as a sample, while `RSK-01` only says "one method per workspace" | BRD lines 994, 1077, 1196, 1216, 1047, 1265; digest lines 1080 to 1084, 1471, 1844 to 1847 | Metric contract version 1 cannot be approved as is, as `D-24` assumes; the reconciliation test cannot cover health; `MCP-10` promises to return health through a tool | Health and the risk score are metric definitions with an id and a version like the other 23 definitions, in the form of threshold rules configured per workspace. The default formula must be approved by the product owner in Discovery before the metric contract is signed |
| BF-02 | Missing | **How votes are combined into the decision of an approval gate.** `GOV-03` only says that a decision cannot be made when quorum is missing. The wireframes show each approver casting one vote with its own value (one picks Rework, one has a draft of Pass with conditions) next to the line "Votes 1/3 · quorum 2/3"; wireframe 49 explains quorum as "3 of 5 approvers must agree". Nowhere does it say whether quorum counts votes cast or votes of the same value, whether a vote can be changed before the gate settles, or how a split vote is handled. `Q-10` (delegation, abstention) is still open | BRD lines 788, 1671; digest lines 916 to 925, 949, 2870 to 2876, 3691 | The rule `BR-42` cannot be written on the server before it is known when an approval gate counts as decided | Each approver is configured with exactly one vote, changeable until the approval gate settles. The approval gate settles when one decision value reaches the quorum vote count. No delegation, no abstention in the first release |
| BF-03 | Missing | **The flow for correcting a decision that has been settled.** `BR-18` and `CHG-11` say a decision is immutable "except through a correction workflow"; wireframe 12 says the correction and the original sit together in the Decision Log. No requirement defines who may make the correction, who must approve, or the state of the stage after the correction | BRD lines 1022, 1275; digest line 937 | This flow needs a command and a permission before immutability can be checked by a test | A correction is a new decision record that points to the original, needs the same authority and quorum as the original decision, and carries a reason. The original never changes. The stage status is recomputed from the latest decision in effect |
| BF-04 | Missing | **The delay (lag) and the conflict inequality of a dependency.** `BLD-15` says a generated dependency keeps both the type and the lag; `WBS-13`, the Dependency entity and the definition of "Dependency conflict" in 12.1 have no lag, do not say whether the later item starting exactly on the day the earlier item ends is a conflict, and do not say whether lag is counted in calendar days or working days | BRD lines 920, 957, 1194, 1348, 1376 | The work item generator and the conflict detector cannot be deterministic without it | A Dependency has a lag field, counted in days on the duration basis of the workspace (`D-07`). The exact inequality for the four link types will be written out in the design section of the WBS tree and awaits the product owner's approval |
| BF-05 | Missing | **The fourth link state and the numbers of slip days.** Section 12.1 only defines conflict and "schedule data incomplete". Wireframe 28 shows a warning that the earlier item is late ("this item cannot start yet", counting "1 waiting") even though the two compared dates do not conflict; wireframes 17 and 19 show the slip days, the buffer zone and the forecast date that spreads downstream ("FS +12d", "FS buffer 10d", "leaves MVP2 at 8 Jul 2027"). There is no definition for forecast, buffer, slip | Digest lines 2168 to 2170, 1296 to 1297, 1483 to 1499 | The impact analysis service (`CHG-03`, `RSK-03`, `RMP-02`) needs these definitions so that two screens do not show two different numbers | Add to the metric definition table: slip is the current target date minus the baseline target date; buffer is the gap between the two ends of a link; the downstream effect is an advisory computation, not written into the data (`BR-23`) |
| BF-06 | Inconsistent | **The channel list.** Section 15.2 lists Web, MCP, API and states that it is not configurable; wireframe 06 filters by Web, MCP, API, System; the addendum records audit entries with the channel "onboarding" | BRD line 1409; digest line 385; addendum lines 322, 545 | The audit envelope must have a single channel enum | Five values: web, mcp, api, system, onboarding |
| BF-07 | Inconsistent | **The MCP tool catalog.** The catalog table has 13 rows holding 17 tool names; wireframe 08 says "13 tools" and "6 of 13 tools allowed". `MCP-05` requires decisions, journal entries, portfolios and workspace configuration to be readable but the catalog has no tool for those four things | BRD lines 835, 854 to 868; digest lines 545, 572 | The versioned catalog (the eighth contract) must fix the number of tools and cover all of `MCP-05` | The canonical catalog counts by tool name (17), and adds read tools for decisions, the journal, portfolios and workspace configuration |
| BF-08 | Ambiguous | **"Not found" and "no access".** `BR-50` and `ONB-23` say these two answers cannot be told apart on any channel; `PLT-04` and wireframe 43 instead require the no-access state to name the project, the role needed and the decision maker when the user is a member of the workspace | Addendum lines 330, 393; BRD line 694; digest lines 3188 to 3198 | The error contract must say clearly at which boundary existence is hidden | Three tiers. Another tenant or not existing: the same not-found answer. Same tenant but not a member of the workspace: no access, with no name or path revealed. A workspace member lacking a project role: no access, with the name, the role needed and the decision maker |
| BF-09 | Contradiction | **Tokens when the tenant is suspended.** `BR-36` says tokens are revoked when the tenant is suspended; `TEN-06` and wireframe 43 say a suspended tenant can still read and export, and the part that is stopped is only listed as "MCP writes" | BRD lines 1293, 725; digest lines 3215 to 3223 | Decides whether read commands through MCP run during suspension, and whether users must re-create tokens after reactivation | Suspension does not delete tokens. Write commands through MCP are rejected with the reason that the tenant is suspended; read commands still run. Mass revocation is a separate action of the tenant admin ("Revoke all" button in wireframe 04, digest line 274) |
| BF-10 | Missing | **Entities that the requirements and wireframes need but section 15.1 does not have:** attention item (`EXE-02`, `BR-09`, `GOV-13`, `ONB-13`); invitation (`PLT-03`); access request (`PLT-04`); the vote of each approver; follow-up conditions and actions after an approval gate (`GOV-15`); health override with a reason (`RSK-04`); strategic link exemption (`CHR-15`); export and import jobs (wireframe 44); deletion record with a recovery period (`PLT-15`); notification preferences (`PLT-09`); work calendar and days off (`WSP-03`); capability and threshold (`RES-02`, `BR-07`); usage counter (`TEN-05`); list of verified clients (`MCP-15`); feature flags and service notices (`TEN-08`); sign-in sessions and trusted devices (`PLT-01`); security events (`ONB-24`) | BRD lines 1334 to 1386 (these entities are absent); addendum lines 702 to 720 | The data model of the spec must add these entities, and the coverage table must be able to point to them | The backend spec lists them in the logical model and marks them "additions to 15.1" |
| BF-11 | Ambiguous | **Writes based on a stale version.** `PLT-06` says a stale version is rejected; section 17.1 says a conflict is only on the same field; wireframe 42 says edits that do not collide are merged automatically. It is unclear whether the server rejects every command based on a stale version and lets the client merge, or the server applies the command itself when the fields do not collide; and what an MCP client sees in the non-colliding case | BRD lines 696, 1475; digest lines 3160, 3170, 3172 | This is the core semantics of the write contract | No assumption set yet. It is a decision for the session, in the group of concurrent writes |
| BF-12 | Missing | **Restoring one tenant.** Section 17.1 and the isolation matrix require restoring one tenant without touching other tenants; `TEN-07` requires that the export package of a tenant can be restored into a new tenant. No requirement covers the import path for a tenant package (who runs it, what is checked); `PLT-14` only imports a project as a new project | BRD lines 726, 746, 1478, 704; digest lines 3319 to 3320 | On shared infrastructure (`D-28`), restoring one tenant must go through exactly this import path | Importing a tenant package is an operation of the provider operator, with a check report before writing, and is the same mechanism as restoring one tenant from a backup |
| BF-13 | Missing | **The Cancelled state of a tenant.** It only says "export window"; it does not say whether sign-in is possible, whether reading is possible, or what happens with MCP | BRD lines 725, 1407; digest line 483 | The permission table by tenant state | Like Suspended, plus a countdown to the deletion date; MCP is switched off completely |
| BF-14 | Missing | **The review step when publishing a lifecycle framework.** `GOV-21` requires review before publish; wireframe 11 has "Submit for review" and says Publish is disabled until the review is approved; the role table only says the Workspace Owner approves the publishing. It does not say who reviews, or whether the reviewer must differ from the author. The addendum treats "AI writes, a human approves" as enough | BRD lines 806, 1309; digest lines 805, 855; addendum line 684 | The permission matrix needs a row for the review action | The publisher must differ from the author of the draft. When the author is an AI, the publisher is the reviewer |
| BF-15 | Ambiguous | **The role table uses wording that cannot be tested:** "within delegated authority", "per policy", "where configured", "within authority". A machine-readable matrix needs concrete thresholds, and `CHG-10` has been moved up to the first release by the addendum | BRD lines 1309 to 1316; addendum lines 688, 780 | Permission tests cannot be generated when a matrix cell is a phrase | Each phrase becomes a workspace policy parameter, with a default value written in the matrix |
| BF-16 | Ambiguous | **The number of keyboard parity matrices.** Section 18.4 names two editors (lifecycle designer, process framework editor); `BR-41` says one matrix per editor; `BLD-04` requires every gesture on the canvas of the Deliverable Builder to have a keyboard equivalent; the front-end spec also declares matrix rows for the WBS tree table | BRD lines 1569, 1298, 946; front-end spec line 623 | The backend must supply a server command column for every matrix | A server command column is supplied for every write operation of five surfaces: lifecycle design, process framework editor, Deliverable Builder, board, WBS tree table |
| BF-17 | Ambiguous | **A node of duration 0 in a process framework.** `BLD-16` allows a duration of 0 and wireframe 58 has a milestone "Day 23, 0d". `WBS-15` defines duration as target date minus start date plus one (minimum 1) and `WBS-11` forbids a target date before the start date. A 0-day node therefore cannot be mapped to the date pair of an item that still "lasts the node duration" as `BLD-14` requires | BRD lines 958, 922, 918, 956; digest line 4359 | The determinism of the work item generator and the constraint consistency check at publish time | No assumption set yet. It will be settled in the design section of the work item generator |
| BF-18 | Terminology mismatch | **"MCP session".** `TEN-02` and the isolation matrix say each "MCP session" belongs to one tenant. The MCP specification version 2026-07-28 that the BRD cites as a source has dropped the connection session and the `initialize` step: each request is self-contained | BRD lines 721, 749; source: modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports, section Backward Compatibility, read on 03/10/2026 | The isolation matrix row for MCP must be written in terms of the token and the request | The boundary is the recipient (audience) of the token, checked on every request. There is no server-side session state |
| BF-19 | Ambiguous | **"Today" in section 12.1** is defined as "the user's date in the workspace timezone", that is both per user and per workspace. For a screen that gathers several workspaces (`OVW-09`) the two can differ | BRD lines 1171, 998 | The "today" reference point decides Overdue and Due today, so it must be a single value | "Today" is the current date in the timezone of the workspace that holds the record; a screen that gathers several workspaces computes each row by the workspace of that row |
| BF-20 | Outdated label | `wireframes/manifest.json` records its convention as "BRD v4.3" while the baseline is v4.5 | manifest line 4 | No effect on the design | No assumption needed |

## 2. Discrepancies between the front-end spec and the backend session (not part of the BRD)

| Id | Content | Evidence | How it is handled in the session |
|---|---|---|---|
| XF-01 | `packages/contracts/openapi/provisional.yaml` does not exist yet; the project folder has no code repo yet and no `packages/` folder | Front-end spec lines 71, 246, 252; the folder listing of 03/10/2026 does not have this file | The locked semantics are taken from front-end spec sections 5.5, 7 and 9.2. The backend is the party that writes the first transport version; the front-end generates mocks from it |
| XF-02 | The front-end spec assigns 34 to 39 people to the front-end teams, while assumption A-07 says about 40 people is the whole agency team | Front-end spec line 667; BRD line 437 | The product owner needs to confirm whether the 40 people are a vertical team doing both sides or there is a separate backend team. It directly affects the language decision for the core |
| XF-03 | The rejection kind `stale` carries only one editor and one time, while wireframe 42 has two edits on two fields in two versions within the same conflict (one by the person editing directly, one by an AI editing through MCP on behalf of that same person). There is no rejection kind yet for hitting a plan limit (`TEN-05`), an approval gate not yet eligible (`BR-42`), loss of write access to the canvas, and a workspace state that does not allow writing | Front-end spec lines 150 to 156, 397; digest lines 3153 to 3160; BRD lines 724, 1299 | Propose the addition openly in the design section of the write contract; no unilateral change |
| XF-04 | `MetricSnapshot.trace` is a list of record ids, while `OVW-04` opens a filtered table and the scale goes up to 2000 items per project, 5000 projects per tenant | Front-end spec line 99; BRD lines 993, 1476 | Proposal in the design section of the metrics engine: the trace carries a reproducible filter together with a count, a list of ids only when small |
| XF-05 | `MetricSnapshot.missing` is a list of project names; `EXE-01` requires naming the projects with missing data, but names must be filtered by the viewer's permissions | Front-end spec line 98; BRD line 1075 | Proposal in the design section of the metrics engine: return ids together with names filtered by permission, plus the number of hidden projects |
